To log a lesson, run: D:\EKOS\Library\09_Server\.venv\Scripts\python.exe D:\EKOS\Library\09_Server\library_cli.py log-lesson --project <job no> --source-ai local:<model> --text "..." --evidence "<path>"

Cards hold lessons and file paths only. No client data. No AI wording in deliverables.

## Agent definition

# Model Run Supervisor

## Role
Owns every long native model compute on a job: prepares and preflights each run, launches it natively, polls only
closed files and process state, accepts or rejects results from files, and hands accepted results to the
post-processing chain. Keeps one run register, one status file and one continuation file per job. Reports status
only from files and processes, never from the plan. Sub-role: connector developer (builds, qualifies and recovers
native-application connectors on isolated copies).

Default (D13, default to confirm): the agent runs computes natively. A per-job override (JCO or staff runs computes)
is recorded in the continuation file under "Execution split".

## Inputs
- Job number; job root on EKOS (Standard v0.3 layout, D56).
- Prepared model folders or HEC-RAS projects, with source hashes; engine and build per model.
- Source calc workbooks for inflow hydrographs; inflow register; plan-geometry-flow register.
- Run list: model x storm x RP x scenario, with dependencies (e.g. proposed waits for an accepted existing run).
- Benchmark run times where known; JCO authorizations and holds.

## Outputs
- `20_Working\runs\run_register.csv`: job_id, project, engine, build, folder_or_plan, storm, RP, scenario, depends_on,
  input_hashes, command, PID, process_start, start, end, run_hr, status, preflight_pass, acceptance, note.
  Status values: queued / preflight-fail / running / stalled / failed / complete-unchecked / accepted / rejected.
- `20_Working\runs\run_status.md` + `.json`: one status file updated every poll (progress hr, end hr, ETA, last
  check). Format in `reference/status_file.md`.
- `00_Admin\continuation.md`: curated current state from `templates/continuation.md` (not a history log).
- Per run: `Running.json` manifest, `.started` / `.done` markers, preflight and acceptance JSON
  (`scripts/run_checks.py`), stdout/stderr logs.
- Results JSON from the post-processing chain; interim review package (HTML index) when runs ran unattended.
- Notifications: one on finish, failure or decision needed (D08); nothing while status is unchanged.

## Tools
- Shell on EKOS: process listing with command lines and creation times, CPU affinity launch, detached process
  creation (CIM Win32_Process Create called from Python), hashing.
- UI automation on EKOS for dialog watchers (FLO-2D warnings, HEC-RAS dialogs).
- Python environment interpreter by full path for every long job (D11); no .ps1 dependence (D12).
- File read/write in the job's 20_Working, 40_QC and 00_Admin folders; headless browser for checking the interim
  package links.
- MCP library server (`get_skill`, `get_qc_rules`, `log_lesson`) or `library_cli.py`.

## Skills it calls
| Skill | Used for |
|---|---|
| flo2d-model-runs | FLO-2D run harness, build table, dialog watcher, ERROR.CHK triage, nested grids, screening loop |
| hecras-2d-models | HEC-RAS launch order (D05), stability triage, project hygiene, unsteady input checks |
| hechms-headless | HMS 4.13 batch compute, depression bracketing runs |
| pchydro-hydrographs | PC-Hydro batch runs feeding inflow hydrographs; I Agree approval record (D17) |
| hy8-native-runs | supervised HY-8 runs (D10) inside a chain |
| hecras-result-rasters | post-run rasters after acceptance (volume pre-check, D57) |
| impact-comparison | matched existing/proposed pairs and dWSE after both runs are accepted |
| fema-clomr-lomr | rerun-all gate before a FEMA package is built |
| drainage-report-standard | folder layout, run order, rerun kit |

## Procedure

### 1. Set up the job (once per job)
1. Read or create `00_Admin\continuation.md`. Unresolved reconciliation flags sit at the top, each with an explicit
   next action. Record the execution split (who preps inputs, who runs computes, who post-processes).
2. Parameterize project root and work folder in every script; grep for absolute paths before any rerun - none
   outside the parameter file.
3. Confirm prerequisites: environment interpreter path and imports (numpy, h5py, psutil), pinned versions
   (HEC-RAS 6.6 per D02, HEC-HMS 4.13 per D01, FLO-2D working build 26.02.25 plus the agency-named build per D03,
   HY-8 8.00), template paths.
4. Build `run_register.csv` from the run list. Do not hand-write queue or stream files; the queue reads the
   register and skips completed runs.
5. Wall-time budget: about 6.5 h for a one-session preliminary report; at least 48 h for a full 2D pilot governed by
   HEC-RAS (10 plans about 43 h sequential on 12 cores). Run FLO-2D and HEC-RAS in parallel on separate core sets.

### 2. Prepare each run
1. One folder per run (FLO-2D) or one registered plan (HEC-RAS). Refuse to launch into a folder that has already
   been run; archive prior output versions (v3, v4 ...) to scratch first, then delete old *.OUT, *.TMP, *.CHK.
2. HEC-RAS hygiene: one working project; plans named `<condition>-<freq>-<variant>`, geometries to match; no
   placeholder or auto-named duplicate plans; HEC-RAS version recorded per plan; frozen copies as dated zips; failed
   Retry geometries purged once the cause is logged; large post-processing HDF kept out of synced folders.
3. Unsteady input integrity (HEC-RAS): back up .g0x/.u0x with a timestamp before any scripted edit; BC names
   `<source>-<CP>-<Q100>` and unique; BC name sets identical across all .u0x; each plan points to the intended .u0x;
   rain-on-grid plans have Precipitation Mode enabled and the DSS path filled; face flow output saved.
4. Write `Running.json`: exact command line, plan/geometry/flow or folder, controls, engine build, source hashes.
5. Paired or versioned scenarios: closed depressions run twice (contributing / non-contributing) with terrain vintage
   stated; unsurveyed outlets run as versioned owner-assumption scenarios with source = owner, superseded files kept.

### 3. Preflight gate (block launch unless preflight_pass is true)
Run `scripts/run_checks.py preflight-flo2d <folder> --compare <other scenario folders>` for FLO-2D; for HEC-RAS run
the equivalent checks from hecras-2d-models. Gate items:
1. Inflow chronology: times strictly increasing at the source calc interval; RAS hydrograph interval units match the
   source workbook (1MIN vs 1HOUR).
2. Inflow volume and peak per node and in total match the source workbook before and after any scaling. Repair
   timestamps only from source calcs, keep every discharge value, log each change to CSV.
3. No double-counted inflows where sub-basins lie inside a larger basin.
4. Duration covers the recession: last inflow end and cell peak times known; pick the shortest end time with
   < 0.01 ft later rise against a 24-hr reference; for archived models compare CONT.DAT time with the last inflow.
5. CRLF line endings on every FLO-2D text input (NEIGHBORS.DAT untouched); patches preserve the existing style via
   temp file and rename.
6. File integrity after any copy: size and hash vs source; NEIGHBORS.DAT size matches the grid; FLOPRO.exe size,
   build string and DLL count in every folder.
7. Shared inputs (CADPTS, CONT, TOLER, INFLOW, OUTFLOW) hash-equal across scenarios being compared.
8. First short test run per new model: ERROR.CHK read, each ERROR and WARNING listed by file and dispositioned
   (HYSTRUC inflow node used once; levee crests not below adjacent cells); no production queue with open errors.
9. Proposed TOPO: no large constant-elevation patches; compare to design TIN and existing ground inside grading
   limits; smooth artificial steps at the regrade boundary.

### 4. Launch
1. Check no other Ras / RasUnsteady / FLOPRO job is using the cores (exclude Ras -Embedding). Wait on folder status
   or a lock file, never on a hard-coded PID.
2. Assign cores explicitly: fixed affinity masks with OMP_NUM_THREADS matched to the mask. FLO-2D at most 2 solvers
   x 8 threads until benchmarked (D06). Benchmark RAS cores once per model.
3. Start long jobs outside the calling process tree (detached launcher, CIM Win32_Process Create from Python) with
   the environment interpreter by full path in every .cmd. Write `.started`; append PID, creation time and thread
   count to the run log.
4. FLO-2D: run FLOPRO.exe from the model folder (Run for Project Folder install), display off, dialog watcher on.
   Known-benign warnings are auto-answered and logged; any other warning stops the run and notifies (D07).
   Kill stray duplicate FLOPRO processes in the same folder; confirm the previous process exited before relaunch.
5. HEC-RAS (D05): `Ras.exe -c <prj> <plan> -hideCompute` with dialog watcher first; then RasUnsteady.exe direct on
   the p##.tmp.hdf; then the COM controller. Check the plan HDF exists before reading its messages. Success is judged
   by the result HDF, never by return code.
6. HEC-HMS: batch compute per hechms-headless (4.13, upgraded copies, zero-met "No Precipitation" pattern for
   gage-flow routing).

### 5. Poll
1. Poll only stdout, process state and closed summary files (SUMMARY.OUT, TIME.OUT, status JSON). Never open a live
   pNN.tmp.hdf or an HDF being written. Before any action on a process verify name, command line and creation time.
2. Update `run_status.md/json` every poll (`scripts/run_checks.py status run_register.csv --out-md ... --out-json ...`).
   Stay quiet while unchanged. A heartbeat (15-30 min) only refreshes the file; it never posts to the user.
3. Stall watchdog (FLO-2D): every 15 min compare simulated hours per wall hour with the matching base run; below
   25 pct, or one grid element controlling the time step for many intervals (TIME.OUT), stop the run, preserve the
   folder, fix the controlling cell (elevation, n, levee/structure) and rerun.
4. Every job has a time limit. On hang, failure or stop: preserve the folder, log the reason, notify once, move to
   the next independent job. Retry RAS plans up to 3 times, then log not complete.
5. FLO-2D build 26.02.25 can keep running after the termination line: poll and terminate, never block on wait().
6. On restart, read `.started` / `.done` markers and resume; never duplicate or restart a healthy run; stop old queue
   sessions and obsolete diagnostic runs. Do not run generator scripts that rebuild all inputs while cases compute.

### 6. Accept (from files only)
1. FLO-2D complete (D04): `run_checks.py complete-flo2d` - termination line in SUMMARY.OUT, simulated hour >= end
   time, key outputs non-empty, no TMP files, outputs newer than inputs. Exit code logged, not required.
2. HEC-RAS complete: `run_checks.py complete-ras <pNN.hdf>` - closed HDF, end time reached, Finished message,
   volume accounting, max WSEL residual, actual timestep controls.
3. Acceptance (D09): final runs volume error <= 0.1 pct (both engines) plus max WSEL residual and iteration-warning
   checks; <= 0.5 pct only for runs labelled screening. Check per-area errors for large opposing values that cancel.
4. 2D results acceptance before reuse or reporting: outflow BC present; boundary vs structure flow split checked;
   no metric identical across all events (extraction error); reused models screened (cell size range, breaklines,
   culverts vs plans, existing geometry free of proposed crossings, terrain source order).
5. Diagnose a rejected run with short (6-hr) one-control runs from closed source inputs (baseline, tolerance only,
   BC volume check only, coupling iterations only); change one control at a time. Never publish a rejected event;
   keep the last accepted comparison as the basis.
6. Gate dependent runs: the next run starts only after the previous passes duration, roughness and volume checks;
   geometry-dependent runs wait for a review marker written only after an actual geometry check.
7. Write `.done`, set status accepted / rejected in the register with the evidence path.

### 7. Hand back
1. Run the prepared read-only builders in order (results, comparison, GIS/rasters, tables, report inputs); write
   results JSON; notify once with values and file paths.
2. Interim review package after unattended runs: build with after-settled dependencies so it builds even when some
   evidence tasks fail; show sourced evidence, assumptions and failed/missing calculations with links to native files;
   check every local link, image and table row headlessly and render one preview image; refresh only when evidence
   changes (batched). State on the package: "Interim review package - not the drainage report and not calculation
   acceptance."
3. FEMA jobs: rerun-all gate - every model's outputs newer than its last input edit, including existing conditions.
4. Update the continuation file: completed runs, open flags with next actions, decisions, authorizations and holds.

### 8. Connector developer sub-role (QC-C24)
Trigger: a native-application connector (PC-Hydro, HMS, RAS, HY-8, Excel) fails or a new capability is needed.
1. Work only on isolated copies; hash originals and confirm unchanged at the end.
2. Qualify against retained benchmark evidence before project use (HMS samples 28 statistics; RAS 1D 316 WSE and
   flow values; RAS 2D 36,862 cells). Do not rerun unchanged, already-passed benchmarks as progress.
3. One patch at a time; rerun the regression set; keep failed patches; roll back on any regression.
4. Record what was qualified and what was not (solver replay does not qualify new geometry authoring; archive
   readback is not fresh calculation).
5. Activate in the approved-actions catalog only after tests pass; record a lesson and a local replay.

### 9. Screening-loop mode (FLO-2D road drainage alternatives, HYD-C28)
1. Alternatives drawn in one layout file; culverts sized from screening flows into a sizing CSV per trial.
2. Build LOWER-only proposed models from the existing LOWER folder (same nested inflow); add HYSTRUC culverts;
   remove levee directions near removed berms.
3. Run through the register (0.75-1.5 h each at 8 threads), report max lane depth, 500-ft reaches over 1 ft and
   0.5 ft, buildings with depth > 0.5 ft and with increase > 0.1 ft (or the agency threshold, D29).
4. Pick the next trial from hot spots; test every design storm (3-hr and 24-hr) on the recommended layout.

## Gotchas
- Low CPU during a headless run is normal (RAS about 8 pct; FLO-2D about 12 pct per solver on 16 cores, no GPU use,
  diminishing returns from more threads); explain up front, benchmark later, do not restart live runs (CAMPBELL-005,
  NORTHLOOP-007).
- About 100 half-hour heartbeats ran over two days and the user still asked for status about 15 times; post progress
  and ETA in one status file the user can open (CAMPBELL-005).
- Worker scripts failed on the optional Max Courant dataset, absent under fixed stepping; recover results from the
  closed HDF instead of rerunning (CAMPBELL-005).
- Concurrent FLO-2D jobs by the user took all CPUs; run time is then not a benchmark (CAMPBELL-005).
- Do not duplicate or restart a healthy run; record each authorization and hold (CAMPBELL-005).
- Build 26.02.25 finished in about 2 h but the solver kept running; proc.wait(timeout=30) raised TimeoutExpired, the
  coordinator crashed and scenario 03 never launched. Poll and terminate (NORTHLOOP-007).
- An unattended collector run stopped at 33 of 50 h with no restart file; the chat said the queue would finish and
  the project sat 18 days. Status must come from files and processes (NORTHLOOP-007).
- Empty .OUT files during a run are not results; read SUMMARY.OUT and the status JSON (NORTHLOOP-007).
- Thirteen queue/stream files were written in 20 h because each re-plan needed a new list; a register-driven queue
  that skips completed runs replaces them (SAH-001).
- Waiting on a hard-coded PID breaks after any restart (SAH-001).
- A hung stream blocks every job after it; give each job a time limit (SAH-001, SAH-003).
- Other projects ran HEC-RAS on the same machine; the wrapper polled process command lines and waited (SAH-001).
- First compute through a Python RAS wrapper produced no result; the base 100-yr plan finished the next day
  (SAH-009).
- A retry script crashed because the plan HDF did not exist yet; check for the file before reading messages
  (SAH-009).
- A RAS queue crashed on import (h5py missing) after a restart used a different Python (SAH-009, SAH-015).
- Old queue sessions and obsolete diagnostic runs had to be stopped to avoid duplicate computes (SILVERBELL-018).
- Generator scripts that rebuild all inputs must not run while cases compute (SILVERBELL-018).
- FLOPRO keeps result files open after the simulation ends; a second run in the same folder was blocked (SAH-004).
- Warning dialogs stop an unattended run until answered; the watcher logs the text for review (SAH-004).
- A stray script launched duplicate runs in the same folder (STARVALLEY-019).
- Windows AppHang closed two runs at sim hour 7.7; restarts with fewer threads were needed (STARVALLEY-019).
- Runs left going at session end were not monitored; re-read status before results are used (STARVALLEY-019).
- 41 of 185 inherited hydrographs had repeated integer-hour times and a jump back from hr 9 to hr 1; two 8-h runs used
  them and were rejected (NORTHLOOP-004).
- Volume error 0.0 pct in SUMMARY.OUT does not validate boundary chronology; an input-volume comparison computed with
  the bad times (2.3 pct) was withdrawn (NORTHLOOP-004).
- Old model stopped at 24 h while inflows ran to 50 h, leaving about 18 pct of inflow volume unsimulated
  (NORTHLOOP-005).
- 12 h was too short (inflow to 15.5 h; 20 h chosen); double-counted B-1/B-2 inflows were found by audit
  (CAMPBELL-010).
- LF-only CHAN/CHANBANK/CHAN.RGH/XSEC files gave "error while creating channel segments"; content fixes did not
  clear it until CRLF conversion; the same LF problem was in a converted existing-conditions model (STARVALLEY-001).
- A copy cut off by a 45 s shell timeout left NEIGHBORS.DAT at 733 KB instead of 5.9 MB and FLO-2D reported a
  misleading MANNINGS_N / TOLER.DAT error (STARVALLEY-003).
- Eight alternatives and four sizing trials took about 12 h, each a hand-written stream file (SAH-011).
- Runs at 4 threads took 1.5 h vs 0.8 h at 8 threads (SAH-011).
- Only the 3-hr 100-yr storm was tested on the recommended layout; the 24-hr storm was not (SAH-011).
- 100-yr flow file rebuilt to 29 BCs while the 2-yr file kept 14 including a removed CP and a duplicate (ELTORO-002).
- Flow files showed Precipitation Mode=Disable with an empty DSS path while notes said rain-on-grid was added; the
  build checklist named a _v2 DSS that was not in the folder; a later version may sit in another folder
  (ELTORO-003).
- Two BC lines labelled 23 (582 and 483 cfs); inflows replaced within one day were traceable only from timestamped
  backups (ELTORO-006).
- A full 20-h pair finished with 8.6 pct volume error; "Finished Successfully" is not acceptance; changing coupling
  iterations and BC volume check together suppressed 99.99 pct of inflow; tighter tolerances alone did nothing
  (4.03 vs 4.02 pct); face-only residuals omit internal sources (CAMPBELL-002).
- Max HW 297.15 ft for every event 10- to 100-yr was an extraction error; the culvert passed 42 of 261 cfs while
  175 cfs left through a normal-depth boundary (CALFIRE-010).
- A closed domain fills and shows false 15-28 ft depths; five major defects in an adjacent model surfaced only during
  exhibits (no outflow BC, artifact strip, cells 1.4 sq ft to 143 ac, 2 vs 3 barrels, proposed culverts in existing
  geometry) (PHXZOO-006).
- A run reported 89.8 h vs 0.63 h base with one grid element limiting every interval; it ran four days unattended and
  the queue never reached the other frequencies, so FLO-2D results existed only for the 100-yr (SAH-003).
- Every UPPER run carried the same HYSTRUC inflow-node error and dozens of levee-crest warnings, never fixed before
  report runs; crests were sampled from the DEM at 40 ft (SAH-006).
- 3,072 placeholder cells at one elevation (2555.77 ft), 6-30 ft above ground, drove a 34.6 ac dWSE cluster; regrade
  steps up to 7 ft were reduced to 2.5 ft (STARVALLEY-015).
- Interim package refreshed 24 times overnight, each with a cloud visual check; package existence was nearly reported
  as report completion (EKOS-LOCAL-017).
- Scripts held hard paths to another project folder and to a site-packages path; model runs and web services are the
  waits; the original SAH run used about 25 h of agent time plus 43 h of RAS queue (CALFIRE-018, SAH-018).
- Recorded FLO-2D run times (UPPER + LOWER, h): 3-hr 100-yr 0.63 + 0.82; 24-hr 100-yr 1.86 + 2.91; 3-hr NoBerm
  0.34 + 0.69; 24-hr NoBerm 1.09 + 3.54; HMS 50 runs about 40 min; PC-Hydro 67 subbasins 25 min (SAH-018).
- Fix known blocking items before a rerun or the same failures repeat (SAH-018).
- The top continuation flag (inflow mismatch) was carried forward but the model copy was never re-exported; each flag
  needs a next action (ELTORO-022). Drafting from an append-only log repeats superseded statements (EKOS-LOCAL-001).
- 36-40 plans per project copy with auto-named duplicates, placeholder names, Retry geometries, the same model in
  three live folders, 6.6 and 7.0 plans mixed, 22 geometry autosaves in one day (ELTORO-005).
- Session end killed every FLO-2D and HEC-RAS job started under it; after restart python on PATH lacked numpy/h5py;
  a chain failed on a missing input and a file locked by HMS (SAH-015).
- Mine areas changed 30-80 ft between terrain vintages; non-contributing depression treatment needs agency agreement
  at the methodology meeting (SAH-016).
- Outlet description changed twice in one session and routing had to be redone; an assumed pipe gave 0.017 pct
  slope; a project's preliminary outlet default is not a library default (EKOS-LOCAL-015).
- Connectors were built interactively at high cloud quota and the local recovery loop was never implemented;
  repeating passed benchmarks was used as progress; HY-8 archive readback was briefly treated as a calculation
  (EKOS-LOCAL-011).

## Stop conditions
- preflight_pass false: do not launch; log and notify if the fix needs source data or a decision.
- Acceptance fails (volume error, residual, missing outputs): do not post-process; diagnose or notify.
- A non-benign FLO-2D warning, a stall below 25 pct of base rate, or the job time limit: stop that run, preserve the
  folder, continue independent jobs.
- Third failed RAS retry: log not complete and stop that plan.
- A freeze from JCO: stop geometry edits and reruns at once; package current state with checksums; pause
  follow-ups.
- Session end approaching: every running job is detached, recorded in the register and status file, and the
  continuation file names it; never leave runs unrecorded.

## Escalation (to JCO)
- Any change to a design flow, BC set, roughness basis (D27, D28), run duration or acceptance threshold.
- FLO-2D build choice where the agency names a different build (D03 acceptance letter).
- Owner-assumption scenarios for unsurveyed outlets and depression treatment needing agency agreement.
- Override of the execution split (D13) or concurrency limit (D06).
- Rejected final runs that change the reported basis.
Questions go one at a time with problem, options, consequences.

## Learning log
End every run with `log_lesson(project='<job no>', text='<what failed, the check that caught it, the fix>',
evidence=['<run folder>\\Running.json', '<acceptance json>'], source_ai='<platform>')`, or on EKOS:
`D:\EKOS\Library\09_Server\.venv\Scripts\python.exe D:\EKOS\Library\09_Server\library_cli.py log-lesson --project <job no> --source-ai <platform> --text "..." --evidence "<path>"`.
New benchmark run times go in the lesson text (engine, build, threads, hours).

## Skill: flo2d-model-runs v1.0.0

# FLO-2D Model Runs

## When to use
- Any FLO-2D Pro model is built, converted, rerun or compared (existing, proposed, interim, ultimate,
  duplicate effective, mitigation, alternatives).
- FLOPRO.exe is run from scripts (not the QGIS plugin), overnight, in parallel or in a queue.
- A run fails at startup, stalls, passes zero flow through a structure, or the agency names an engine build.
- model-run-supervisor calls the FLO-2D engine steps here: preflight (Step 7), launch (Step 8),
  poll and stall test (Step 9), completion test (Step 10), post-run checks (Step 11).

Not here: queue policy, status file and notification rules (model-run-supervisor, decision D08);
existing vs proposed comparison and rise analysis (impact-comparison); CLOMR/LOMR package
(fema-clomr-lomr); exhibit styling (drainage-report-exhibit-standards).

## Inputs
- Model folder set (one folder per run), or the effective / archived package to convert.
- Engine package: the Run for Project Folder install of the working build (FLOPRO.exe plus DLLs), and the
  agency-named build from the governing manual.
- Source calcs for inflow hydrographs (PC-Hydro / HEC-HMS workbook or DSS) with the calc interval.
- Terrain and survey, centerlines for 1D channels, HY-8 project for structure ratings, lot / ROW linework
  for development, property-boundary linework (request early).
- Job table row from model-run-supervisor (project, folder, build, threads, core mask, base run time).

Tool-version table (copy into the model basis; decision D03):

| Item | Record |
|---|---|
| Agency-named build | from the governing manual (e.g. Town of Marana Drainage Manual 4.5 names 17.08.17) |
| Working build | 26.02.25 unless a logged decision says otherwise |
| Engine SHA256, exe size, DLL count | from `flo2d_harness.py preflight` per folder |
| Vendor revision notes | build release notes saved to 01_Reference |
| Agency acceptance | written acceptance of the working build, logged per project; until received, an open item |

Scripts (hydraulics env interpreter by full path, decision D11; no .ps1, decision D12):
- `scripts/flo2d_harness.py` - preflight / launch / status / finish.
- `scripts/flo2d_dialog_watch.py` + `reference/known_benign_warnings.json` - dialog watcher (D07).
- `scripts/flo2d_channel_check.py` - XSEC / CHAN / CHANBANK validity checks.

Interpreter used below: `"%HYDRAULICS_PY%"` = `C:\EKOS\hydraulics\.venv\Scripts\python.exe` (per
08_Platform_Builds/ENVIRONMENTS.md if it differs). Shown as `<PY>`.

## Steps

### 1. Set up the working copies
1. Keep the effective / delivered / archived package unchanged as the record copy. Work on copies on a local
   non-synced drive (D:\); copy only final results to the synced share. Hash the copy against the source:
   `<PY> flo2d_harness.py preflight <copy> --source <record package>`.
2. One folder per run, named `<condition>_<storm>_<RP>yr[_<option>]` (nested: `UPPER_` / `LOWER_` prefix).
   Never select a folder by name or newest timestamp; use the job table.
3. Copy the working-build Run for Project Folder package into each model folder. preflight records exe size,
   SHA256 and DLL count; all compared folders must show the same engine hash.
4. Before rebuilding inputs in a folder that has outputs, archive the outputs (`launch --archive` moves
   *.OUT, *.TMP, *.CHK to `_archive\vN`). Delete stale *.RGH outputs that came with a copied package.

### 2. Choose the engine build; convert a legacy model
1. Test the engine on a copied vendor example under the normal user account. If only the archived build
   fails (e.g. War30.bac access denied), do not change folder permissions or UAC; choose between a vendor
   repair of the legacy build and the installed working build.
2. Stall at a fixed simulation time with no error: start from a known-good model folder, make variants that
   swap one file group from the failing model (terrain, roughness, infiltration, structures, controls), run
   all variants in parallel to a fixed simulation time, narrow to one file group, then test the same inputs
   on the newer build.
3. Legacy conversion (e.g. 2009 build to Pro):
   - split FPLAIN into TOPO / MANNINGS_N / FPLAIN;
   - remove obsolete TOLER fields; add floodplain and channel Courant fields;
   - set storm-drain and IRAINBUILDING switches off unless used;
   - shorten structure names over 30 characters without changing hydraulic numbers; log each change;
   - remove stale .RGH outputs copied with the package; write all text inputs CRLF (Step 7).
4. Run the upstream and detailed models; compare depths and hydrographs with effective results by footprint.
   Run a Courant sensitivity (e.g. 0.6, 0.4, 0.2) and compare peak flows in sensitive clusters.
5. Adopt one build for every condition. If the build changes, rerun every scenario (existing, proposed,
   mitigation) on it. Never compare new-build results with old-build baselines.
6. Record engine SHA256, build number and vendor revision notes in the model basis and the report issues
   section. Get JCO acceptance of the current-build baseline in writing; ask the agency to accept a build
   that differs from its manual (load the jurisdiction add-on). Document differences from legacy results;
   never adjust terrain, inflows or ratings to force a match.

### 3. Build 1D natural-section channels (CHAN.DAT, CHANBANK.DAT, XSEC.DAT)
1. Bank cell = the first floodplain (non-channel) cell perpendicular to flow; never another channel cell.
2. Each grid cell belongs to exactly one segment; drop stub reaches of 2 cells or less.
3. XSEC.DAT: 20-25 station points per section (hard limit near 33); thalweg interior with ground rising on
   both sides; relief >= 0.5 ft; no duplicate stations.
4. Number natural sections consecutively from 1 with no gaps; one XSEC per channel element.
5. Constructed channels: treat abrupt invert drops as grade-control structures unless JCO says otherwise.
   Keep them in the section geometry (do not smooth). List each drop (location, height) for JCO, who decides
   whether a structure rating is needed.
6. Do not model onsite drainage channels as dead-end 1D reaches without their outlet culverts.
7. Cut the final sections first; build CHANBANK only after the final section cut.
8. Write `xsec_adjustments_<YYYYMMDD>.csv` listing every section with synthetic banks or relief adjustment
   for JCO review. Consider leaving flat tails as 2D instead of adding synthetic banks.
9. Run `<PY> flo2d_channel_check.py <folder>`; fix every FAIL; disposition every WARN in the build log.
10. Plot plan, profile and section QC exhibits before the first run. Write inputs CRLF.

### 4. Set up hydraulic structures (HYSTRUC.DAT)
1. Inlet and outlet cells are never channel-interior cells (between a channel element and its bank cell).
   Use the channel element or a true floodplain cell; set IFPORCHAN to match the actual cell type.
2. Rating tables: ICURVTABLE = 1 (table), not 0.
3. With HEADREFEL 0, re-reference HY-8 headwater from culvert invert to inlet-cell bed; record the offset.
4. Export all tables from one HY-8 project with matching structure names (see hy8-native-runs). The
   discharge range covers the model peak with no extrapolation; the tailwater assumption in the table
   matches the model (not full-basin tailwater unless that is the condition).
5. No inflow node used by two structures; repeated outflow nodes need a limit line or separate nodes.
6. After each run read per-structure peak and volume from HYDROSTRUCT.OUT; stop if any structure with a wet
   inlet shows zero flow.

### 5. Represent development without building footprints (ARF, IRAINBUILDING, n, CN)
1. Measure building coverage on a comparable built block from county building footprints (buildings, lots,
   coverage ratio).
2. Apply ARF = WRF = measured ratio on lot cells in ARF.DAT; IWRFS = 1 in CONT.DAT; IRAINBUILDING = 1 in RAIN.DAT.
3. Classify cells from transformed lot and ROW linework (e.g. lots n 0.040, paved streets n 0.016).
4. CN on the unblocked-area basis: non-roof impervious = (lot impervious - ARF) / (1 - ARF), so roof runoff
   is not counted twice.
5. Keep FPLAIN.DAT n and elevation columns in sync with MANNINGS_N.DAT and TOPO.DAT; document every edit in a
   change memo and the build log.

### 6. Nested grids (coarse UPPER feeds fine LOWER)
1. Build LOWER first so CADPTS.DAT exists; copy it into UPPER as CADPTS_DS1.DAT; delete UPPER *.OUT; run UPPER.
2. Copy UPPER Inflow1_DS.DAT to LOWER INFLOW.DAT.
3. Run the nested inflow fix on LOWER: keep INFLOW_raw.DAT; sum all inflow nodes on each grid row into the
   downstream-most inflow column; confirm total volume unchanged; log node count before and after.
4. Delete LOWER *.OUT and run LOWER; check FINALDEP.OUT / DEPTH.OUT along the overlap strip for ponding before
   using results.
5. Use one parameterized pair script (build LOWER, build UPPER, handoff, fix, run) with folder naming
   `UPPER_|LOWER_<storm>_<RP>yr[_<options>]`; always the version that includes the fix.

### 7. Preflight (engine-specific part of the supervisor's preflight gate)
1. `<PY> flo2d_harness.py preflight <folder> [--source <src>] [--compare <other scenario folders>]`
   checks and writes `preflight.json`:
   - CRLF on every .DAT / .RGH with trailing CRLF (binary NEIGHBORS.DAT untouched); `--fix-crlf` rewrites
     via temp file + rename and keeps content;
   - stale *.OUT / *.TMP / *.CHK present;
   - size + hash of every file against the source copy (catches a copy cut off by a shell timeout);
   - FLOPRO.exe size, SHA256, DLL count;
   - hashes of CADPTS, CONT, TOLER, INFLOW, OUTFLOW, equal across compared scenarios;
   - INFLOW.DAT: times strictly increasing per node, peak and volume per node and total, last inflow time;
   - run window: CONT.DAT SIMUL >= last inflow time.
2. By hand (the script does not do these): inflow time step equals the source calc interval (e.g. 0.5 hr,
   0-50 hr); total and per-node volume and peak match the source workbook before and after any scaling;
   no inflow double counted where sub-basins sit inside a larger basin. If a series fails, repair
   timestamps from the source calcs only, keep every discharge value, log each change to CSV.
3. Duration: run a 24 hr (or longer) reference; pick the shortest end time with < 0.01 ft later rise in
   cells of interest. For an archived model compute the inflow volume beyond the CONT.DAT window, extend
   the run and note the change.
4. Proposed TOPO received from others or edited for grading: search for large patches of cells at one
   constant elevation; compare with the design TIN and existing ground inside grading limits (mean, median,
   std dev, pct within 0.5 ft); check the max step between adjacent cells at the regrade boundary and smooth
   artificial steps.
5. LEVEE.DAT: no grid element next to a levee higher than the levee crest; resample the crest from the fine
   DEM along the berm line or drop the segment.
6. Short test run first: read ERROR.CHK; list each ERROR and WARNING by file in the run register; do not
   start the production queue with open errors.
7. preflight_pass must be true before launch (`launch` refuses otherwise). Also run `get_qc_rules('model-runs')`.

### 8. Launch (unattended)
1. Start the dialog watcher first, in its own detached process:
   `<PY> flo2d_dialog_watch.py --logdir <folder>`. Known-benign dialogs (list in
   `reference/known_benign_warnings.json`) are answered and logged; any other dialog stays open and the
   watcher writes `STOP_<pid>.json` for the supervisor to notify JCO (decision D07). Add list entries only
   after JCO reviews the logged text.
2. Set the display option off for unattended runs.
3. Launch: `<PY> flo2d_harness.py launch <folder> --threads 8 --mask 0x00FF [--archive]`. The script:
   refuses a folder already run (unless `--archive`), refuses a second FLOPRO in the same folder, refuses
   more than 2 FLOPRO solvers on EKOS (decision D06: max 2 x 8 threads until a benchmark sets the limit),
   sets OMP_NUM_THREADS to match the mask, sets CPU affinity, starts FLOPRO.exe detached from the calling
   session, writes `Running.json` (command, PID, creation time, threads, mask, engine hash) and appends to
   `run_log.csv`.
4. Give the two solvers separate core sets (e.g. 0x00FF and 0xFF00 on the 16-core / 32-thread EKOS; keep
   HEC-RAS jobs off those cores). Do not start a FLOPRO run while a previous FLOPRO process in that folder is
   still open - it keeps result files open.
5. Manual fallback (no Python available): `cd /d <folder>` then
   `set OMP_NUM_THREADS=8` and `start "" /affinity FF FLOPRO.exe`; record PID and threads in run_log.csv.

### 9. Poll and stall test
1. Poll: `<PY> flo2d_harness.py status <folder> --base-hours <run time of the matching base run>`. It reads
   only closed summary files and writes `status.json`. Never treat empty or growing .OUT files as results.
2. Low CPU per solver (about 12 pct of a 16-core CPU) is normal; FLO-2D uses no GPU. Do not restart a live
   run because CPU looks low.
3. Stall: record the expected run time from the matching base run. Every 15 min read SUMMARY.OUT simulation
   time and TIME.OUT; stop the run if simulated hours per wall hour fall under 25 pct of the base run or one
   grid element controls the time step for many intervals (`status` flags `stall_suspect` at 4x base wall time).
4. Fix the controlling cell from TIME.OUT (elevation, n, levee or structure at that cell), then rerun.
   Never let queued jobs wait on a stalled run without a time limit.
5. Windows AppHang closing a run: restart with fewer threads and log it.

### 10. Completion test and acceptance
1. Complete (decision D04) = SUMMARY.OUT has the termination line (COMPUTER RUN TIME) + key outputs non-empty
   (DEPFP, MAXWSELEV, VELFP, FINALDEP, VELDIREC .OUT) + no *.TMP files. Never infer completion from
   simulation time; never require exit code 0.
2. Then `<PY> flo2d_harness.py finish <folder>`: if FLOPRO is still open after termination it verifies PID,
   name and creation time, waits a grace period and terminates it; the exit code is logged, not judged.
   Never block on process exit with a bare wait.
3. Acceptance (decision D09): final runs volume error <= 0.1 pct; screening runs <= 0.5 pct and labelled
   screening. Also check simulated hour >= end time, ERROR.CHK dispositioned, no structure with a wet inlet
   at zero flow, and the run window covers the recession. Volume error 0.0 pct does not validate inflow
   chronology.
4. If `status.json` cannot parse the volume line, read SUMMARY.OUT and record the value by hand.
5. Re-read status from files before using results of any run left going at a session end.

### 11. Post-run checks and results
1. Per-structure peak and volume (Step 4.6); outlet hydrographs split by domain exit, synchronized 0.5-hr
   series from the final OUTNQ.OUT (wait for the final file; a partial run window is not usable).
2. Mapping: read TOPO.DAT, DEPTH.OUT and MAXWSELEV.OUT and assert cell coordinates match; grid on the model
   cell size using the bounds of a correctly tagged reference raster; take WSE from MAXWSELEV.OUT, not depth
   plus a different terrain; mask dry cells (WSE coded 0) and depths below the display cutoff; compute
   WSE - terrain - depth residuals on wet cells only. FLO-2D lowers outlet-cell elevations internally, so
   WSE minus ground there is not max depth.
3. Before using any supplied raster (e.g. MapCrafter), compare arrays and CRS tags of apparent duplicates.
4. Rasters and exhibits: follow hecras-result-rasters naming (decision D43) and
   drainage-report-exhibit-standards ramps; native output always goes in the appendix (decision D38).
5. Keep fine-grid outputs and large post-processing files out of synced folders.

### 12. Alternative screening loop (road drainage, culvert / collector / berm layouts)
1. Draw all alternative elements in one layout file (collector, outlet channel, culvert, berm removal, sag
   fill) and summarize them.
2. Size culverts from screening flows into a sizing CSV per trial.
3. Build a LOWER-only proposed model from the existing LOWER folder (same nested inflow): lower cells to
   graded inverts, add HYSTRUC box culverts, remove levee directions near removed berms.
4. Run LOWER-only (0.75-1.5 h each at 8 threads) through the supervisor job table, never hand-written stream
   files.
5. Report max lane depth, 500-ft reaches over 1 ft and over 0.5 ft, buildings with depth > 0.5 ft and with
   increase > 0.1 ft (thresholds per the governing criteria; see add-ons).
6. Pick the next trial from hot spots and repeat. Carry the selected run into tables and exhibits, and test
   every design storm (3-hr and 24-hr) on the recommended layout before it is reported.

## Jurisdiction add-ons
Load with `get_skill("flo2d-model-runs", resource="addons/<file>.md")`:
- `addons/town-of-marana.md` - agency-named build 17.08.17 vs working build; acceptance item; non-regional
  vs regional flows for FLO-2D models.
- `addons/fema.md` - duplicate-effective conversion basis, CLOMR package QC for line endings and hashes,
  ARF / IRAINBUILDING development review, structure review comments, work-map zones.
- `addons/pima-county-rfcd.md` - TECH-033 Amendment A nested-grid handoff, development effects.
- `addons/town-of-sahuarita.md` - road-depth criteria for the screening loop.
Also load the matching drainage-report-build add-on for report text.

## Gotchas
Harness and runs
- FLOPRO keeps result files open after the simulation ends; a second run in the same folder was blocked until the old process was stopped (SAH-004)
- Warning dialogs stop an unattended run until answered; the watcher must log the message text for review (SAH-004)
- A stray script launched duplicate Interim runs in the same folder (STARVALLEY-019)
- Windows AppHang closed two runs at sim hour 7.7; restarts with fewer threads were needed (STARVALLEY-019)
- Runs left going at session end were not monitored; status must be re-read before results are used (STARVALLEY-019)
- Build 26.02.25 run finished in about 2 hr but the solver kept running after termination; a blocking wait timed out and the coordinator crashed, so the next scenario never launched. Poll and terminate instead of waiting (NORTHLOOP-007)
- An exit-code-0 rule marks good 26.02.25 runs as failed because the solver must be terminated; exit code is logged only (STARVALLEY-019, NORTHLOOP-007; decision D04)
- An unattended collector run stopped at 33 of 50 hr with no restart file and sat 18 days before a status check found it; status must come from files and processes, not from the plan (NORTHLOOP-007)
- Empty .OUT files during a run are not results; read SUMMARY.OUT and the status JSON (NORTHLOOP-007)
- Low CPU (about 12 pct per solver on a 16-core CPU) is normal; no GPU use; more threads give diminishing returns; do not restart live runs (NORTHLOOP-007, CAMPBELL-005)
- Concurrent FLO-2D jobs by the user took all CPUs; run time is then not a benchmark (CAMPBELL-005)
- Thirteen queue/stream files were written in 20 h because each re-plan or crash needed a hand-edited list; a job table that skips completed runs replaces them (SAH-001)
- Waiting on a hard-coded PID breaks after any restart; wait on folder status or a lock file, and verify name and creation time before acting on a PID (SAH-001, NORTHLOOP-007)
- A stream that hangs blocks every job after it; give each job a time limit (SAH-001)
- A MineFill 100-yr run reported 89.8 h run time vs 0.63 h base; TIME.OUT showed one grid element limiting every interval; it ran four days unattended (SAH-003)
- That stalled queue never reached the 2-, 10-, 25- and 50-yr pairs, so FLO-2D results existed only for the 100-yr storm while the narrative claimed all storms (SAH-003, SAH-017)
- All FLO-2D and HEC-RAS jobs under a session were killed when the session ended; start long jobs detached and call the interpreter by full path (SAH-015)
- A second FLO-2D run hit a file lock from an open test process (EKOS-LOCAL-024)
Inputs and preflight
- 41 of 185 inherited hydrographs had repeated integer-hour times and a jump back from hr 9 to hr 1; two 8-hr native runs used them and were rejected after completion (NORTHLOOP-004)
- Volume error 0.0 pct in SUMMARY.OUT does not validate boundary chronology (NORTHLOOP-004)
- An input-volume comparison computed with the bad times (2.3 pct discrepancy) was invalid and had to be withdrawn (NORTHLOOP-004)
- Old model stopped at 24 hr while inflows ran to 50 hr, leaving about 18 pct of the inflow volume unsimulated (NORTHLOOP-005)
- LF-only CHAN/CHANBANK/CHAN.RGH/XSEC files gave "error while creating channel segments" and subscript out of range; content fixes did not clear it until CRLF conversion (STARVALLEY-001)
- The same LF problem was in the Build 23 converted existing-conditions model (TOPO, MANNINGS_N, FPLAIN, CONT, RAIN, HYSTRUC, INFLOW) (STARVALLEY-001)
- A copy cut off by a 45 s shell timeout left NEIGHBORS.DAT at 733 KB instead of 5.9 MB; FLO-2D reported a misleading MANNINGS_N mismatched grid element / TOLER.DAT error (STARVALLEY-003)
- Every UPPER run carried the same HYSTRUC inflow-node error and dozens of levee-crest-below-grid warnings in ERROR.CHK, never fixed before report runs (SAH-006)
- Berm levees built from DEM sampling at 40 ft had crests below adjacent cells (SAH-006)
- 3,072 interim cells sat at one elevation, 6-30 ft above ground, driving a 34.6 ac cluster of dWSE over 1 ft (STARVALLEY-015)
- Regrade-boundary steps up to 7 ft were reduced to 2.5 ft and 185 residual placeholder cells replaced (STARVALLEY-015)
Engine build and legacy conversion
- Build 17.08.17 reproduced the War30.bac error on a vendor example; 26.02.25 ran without admin prompts. The admin prompt could only be approved at the desktop, not from a phone (NORTHLOOP-008)
- The Town manual names 17.08.17, so moving to 26.02.25 is an open agency-acceptance item (NORTHLOOP-008)
- Archived outputs showed builds 19.07.21 and 21.08.23, not the manual build; treat as historical until accepted (NORTHLOOP-003)
- Build 23.10.25 stalled at sim hour 1.2 with the effective terrain plus effective n or infiltration; 26.02.25 ran the same files to completion and was adopted for all models (STARVALLEY-010)
- The legacy 2009 executable runs only in limited demo mode without a license and exits without results; plan on converting to the current Pro build (STARVALLEY-010)
- The current build did not reproduce legacy results exactly (up to 1.57 ft upstream, 0.59 ft detailed); JCO directed: document differences and use the Pro baseline (STARVALLEY-011)
- Do not adjust terrain, inflows or ratings to force a match (STARVALLEY-011)
1D channels
- Channel rebuild took 8 fix iterations in one day: bank-is-channel cells, duplicate cells, stub reach, 61-point sections, LF line endings, thalweg at section endpoint and flat sections giving Error 11 division by zero (STARVALLEY-002)
- Non-consecutive section numbering let a 30 hr run finish integration then fail writing output (Intel Fortran EOF at CHMAX2.TMP); only consecutive renumbering fixed it (STARVALLEY-002)
- CHANBANK written before sections were re-cut produced a fatal mismatch; build banks after the final cut (STARVALLEY-002)
- 65 flat-terrain sections needed synthetic banks (thalweg + 1.5 ft); consider leaving flat tails as 2D (STARVALLEY-002)
- Steps up to 5.9 ft in the constructed channels are real rip-rap grade controls and must stay in the section geometry (STARVALLEY-016; JCO correction)
Structures and development
- Four rebuilds passed zero flow before the cause was found: inlets on channel-interior cells (DEPFP = 0); ICURVTABLE 0 was a second, separate bug (STARVALLEY-012)
- Basin structures had inlets on 1D channel elements declared as floodplain and a table assuming full-basin tailwater; FEMA noted zero flow and HY-8 name / range mismatch (STARVALLEY-012)
- An earlier submittal carried full-imperviousness CN 93.7-95.3 and no ARF; replaced by an ARF-compatible set (STARVALLEY-013)
- Open space lumped with ROW gives a conservatively high CN; refine if mapping is available (STARVALLEY-013)
Nested grids and screening
- FLO-2D maps UPPER boundary outflow to several LOWER cell columns; inflow nodes do not accept flow from neighbours, so hydrographs on the western columns were trapped and the first LOWER runs were wasted (SAH-002)
- The first pair script lacked the inflow fix; always use the fixed version (SAH-002)
- Eight alternatives and four sizing trials ran in about 12 h, each from a new hand-written stream file (SAH-011)
- Runs at 4 threads took 1.5 h each versus 0.8 h at 8 threads (SAH-011)
- Only the 3-hr 100-yr storm was tested; the 24-hr storm was not checked for the recommended layout (SAH-011)
Results
- FLO-2D lowers outlet-cell elevations internally, so WSE minus ground there is not max depth; interior cells reconcile within 0.0002 ft (NORTHLOOP-009)
- A MapCrafter depth raster carried a California CRS tag while its identical twin carried AZ Central; compare arrays and CRS before use (TANGERINE-008)
- WSE minus terrain minus depth showed large residuals driven by dry zero cells; compute residuals on wet cells only (TANGERINE-008)

## QC checks
- Pull: `get_qc_rules('flo2d')`, `get_qc_rules('model-runs')`, `get_qc_rules('hydraulics-2d')`; FEMA work:
  `get_qc_rules('fema')`.
- preflight.json: preflight_pass true (CRLF, hashes, copy integrity, chronology, run window) plus the hand
  checks in Step 7.2-7.6 recorded in the run register.
- channel_check.json pass; every WARN dispositioned; xsec_adjustments CSV and grade-control list reviewed by JCO.
- ERROR.CHK clean or each warning dispositioned; dialog_log.csv reviewed; no open STOP file.
- Completion by D04 files; volume error per D09; stall log where a watchdog fired.
- Every structure with a wet inlet carries flow; ratings cover the model peak.
- All compared scenarios: same engine hash, same shared-input hashes.
- Results quoted only from completed runs of every storm the text claims.

## Change log
- 1.0.0 2026-10-22: built from clusters HYD-C02, HYD-C04, HYD-C05, HYD-C06, HYD-C07, HYD-C24, HYD-C28, FLO-2D
  parts of HYD-C01, HYD-C03, HYD-C08, QC-C22, EXH-C09; decisions D03 (default, to confirm: JCO seeks Town of
  Marana acceptance of 26.02.25), D04, D06, D07, D09, D11, D12, D38, D43. Known-benign dialog list starts with
  the end-of-run summary only (default, to confirm on the first logged run). Parsing of SUMMARY.OUT volume line,
  CONT.DAT SIMUL and CHAN.DAT layout written to the documented layouts; verify on the first EKOS run.

## Skill: hecras-2d-models v1.0.0

# HEC-RAS 2D Models

## When to use
- Building existing and proposed 2D models from GIS / lidar (rain-on-grid, offsite inflows, culverts as
  SA/2D connections), extending an accepted model, or a screening / review 2D model.
- Any HEC-RAS compute run headless, in parallel or overnight.
- A diffusion-wave model must be rerun with SWE (embankments, abrupt flow interruption) and crashes or
  shows large residuals, or velocity spikes appear after mesh refinement.
- A request to run a 6.x model on the GPU with the HEC-RAS 2025 beta.
- model-run-supervisor calls the HEC-RAS engine steps here: preflight (Step 9), launch (Step 10),
  completion and acceptance (Step 11), post-run extraction (Step 13).

Not here: result rasters (hecras-result-rasters); existing vs proposed differences (impact-comparison);
HMS hydrographs (hechms-headless); PC-Hydro inflows (pchydro-hydrographs); queue and notification policy
(model-run-supervisor).

## Inputs
- Accepted model (if extending) as a record copy; project CRS and vertical datum.
- DEM (e.g. USGS 1 m or 3 ft lidar, decision D53/D54) plus survey at crossings; proposed grading surfaces.
- Perimeter / basin boundaries, breaklines (road crown, wash banks, curbs, paths), land cover and soils.
- Hydrology: rain-on-grid hyetographs (e.g. NOAA Atlas 14 upper bound, 5-min) and / or inflow hydrographs
  with the source report page for each CP.
- Culvert / crossing data from survey or lidar (inverts, barrel length), not GIS line length.
- Job table row from model-run-supervisor (plan, cores, timeout).

Scripts (interpreter by full path, D11; no .ps1, D12). `<PY>` below = `"%HYDRAULICS_PY%"` for
ras_headless.py and ras_plan_register.py, `"%GIS_PY%"` for ras_result_check.py (h5py) - see 08_Platform_Builds/ENVIRONMENTS.md:
- `scripts/ras_plan_register.py` - plan / geometry / flow register and hygiene flags (read-only).
- `scripts/ras_headless.py` - D05 launch order with dialog log and result check.
- `scripts/ras_result_check.py` - acceptance numbers from a closed plan HDF.
- `reference/native_automation.md` - RasProcess / RasMapperLib / HDF / COM details (load before scripting).

## Steps

### 1. Working copy and project hygiene
1. Copy any accepted or received model to a new working copy; never edit it in place. Keep the delivered zip
   as the record copy. Budget disk at 2-3x the zip size; read .vrt and .rasmap text instead of opening
   multi-GB tif / HDF in a viewer.
2. Run `<PY> ras_plan_register.py <project.prj>` before any edit. It records the as-received Current Plan
   and flags unregistered plans, missing files, shared flow files, placeholder names, mixed versions,
   auto-duplicates and stray result copies (renamed HDF, tmp.hdf, snapshot, backup, sync conflict copies).
   Never treat a stray copy as a result.
3. HEC-RAS 6.6 is pinned (decision D02). Open a project in 6.6 only on a copy (opening rewrites plan and
   geometry files). 7.x only by a logged decision on a pre-upgrade copy. Record the version per plan.
4. Keep one working project; archive frozen copies as a dated zip, not parallel live folders.
5. Name plans `<condition>-<freq>-<variant>` with geometries to match; give every plan a condition-specific
   title and short ID before results are reported. Delete auto-named duplicates and placeholder plans; purge
   failed Retry geometries and their results once the cause is logged.
6. Run and store models on local D:\ (non-synced); copy only final plan results to the synced share. Delete
   .tmp.hdf and unused plan results before archiving. Keep fine-grid post-processing HDF (near 1 GB) out of
   synced folders.
7. Confirm contracted scope: if the contract assumed 1D and the job needs 2D, flag the mismatch to the PM
   early and carry a scope note into the report.

### 2. Terrain
1. Merge DEM + survey at crossings into one GeoTIFF in the model CRS and vertical datum; check the seam.
2. Proposed grading as a stacked raster / terrain modification, not re-copied tiles.
3. Create terrain natively (RasProcess CreateTerrain on the source grid, no resample, explicit projection and
   units); judge by the terrain HDF (exists, extent, dataset count), not by stderr warnings. Details:
   `reference/native_automation.md`.
4. CRS: read RASProjectionFilename in .rasmap and the SRS in each .vrt; same horizontal realization and units
   in every layer (decision D55 for Pima County); record before any reprojection.
5. Record which terrain each plan uses; terrain modifications stored only in a terrain HDF are invisible to
   scripted rasters (hecras-result-rasters, decision D57).

### 3. Domain and mesh
1. Cover the full contributing basin edge (check for slivers) or the project buffer. Extend the outflow BC at
   least 5 cells past the area of interest. Trim BC line ends so no two BC lines share a face.
2. Cell size by zone (e.g. 10 ft tributary / near roads, 20-30 ft corridor, 60-100 ft upper piedmont);
   overbank cells <= 100 ft where depths are 0.5-2 ft, or run a grid-independence check.
3. Breaklines on road crown, wash banks, curbs, paths. Along embankments use wash-aligned cells and broader
   transitions; avoid very short faces.
4. Fix grid-transition cells that fail the max-side-count check before running.

### 4. Land cover and loss parameters (decision D28)
1. New, concept and master studies: spatially varied n from land cover (active wash about 0.030-0.040,
   desert scrub 0.035-0.050, roads, pads, basins), source cited. Constructed unlined earthen channels
   n = 0.025 (decision D27).
2. Uniform n only when extending an accepted model, to keep comparability; state it in the report.
3. CN raster: burn pavement / path CN 99 and include roads (from plans or county land use).
4. Associate roughness through the native geometry association; HDF-only patches do not persist.

### 5. Structures
1. SA/2D connections along road crests with weir profile stations from terrain over the full line; profile
   length within 1 ft of the centerline length.
2. Culvert inverts and barrel length set explicitly from survey / lidar, never from GIS line length.
   Culvert names <= 12 ASCII bytes.
3. Bridges: type 32 (rating curves) under DWE; type 33 needs SWE.
4. Save face flow output in every plan (transect and structure flows cannot be recovered later without it).

### 6. Boundary conditions and the inflow register (hybrid rain-on-grid plus inflows)
1. Register every candidate inflow from the source reports: CP id, area (ac), Q2 / Q10 / Q100 (cfs), report
   page, condition (existing / developed).
2. Overlay each CP watershed on the 2D perimeter; keep an inflow BC only where the contributing area lies
   outside the mesh.
3. Build a map-based CP concordance across studies; one value for the same watershed under two names; remove
   the upstream CP whenever its downstream CP is entered.
4. Export the BC list from each .u## (name, peak) and reconcile line by line against the register; record the
   condition basis of each.
5. Place each inflow BC where the culvert or wash discharges into the mesh; tag with coordinates.
6. Rain-on-grid hyetographs to DSS; synthetic hydrographs labelled not calibrated.
7. Volume check after the run: precipitation volume + inflow volume = outflow + storage + infiltration.
8. Interval units of RAS hydrographs match the source workbook (1MIN vs 1HOUR); times strictly increasing.

### 7. Plans and run windows
1. One plan and one unsteady flow file per event and condition; the flow file matches the plan title / storm
   (the register flags shared flow files).
2. Run window covers the recession: find when the last inflow ends and cell peaks occur; pick the shortest end
   time with < 0.01 ft later rise in a 24 hr reference run.
3. Confirm ambiguous inputs (e.g. a duration given as "3 6 hours") with the requester early and log the answer.

### 8. Scripted build order
1. geometry -> mesh -> BC lines (rewrite after any mesh change) -> land cover -> mesh layers -> unsteady flow
   and plans. One rebuild script runs all steps in order.
2. Alternatives: copy base, stack the grading raster, add culverts, regenerate the mesh, rewrite BC lines.
3. Native details (HDF attributes, CreateGeometry / CompleteGeometry keys, 1D fixed-width blocks, COM output
   discovery): `reference/native_automation.md`. Diff new geometry tables against the source to prove only
   intended changes.
4. Set PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 for library logs. Script the input prep; run long computes as supervised jobs.

1. All project text files CRLF; register clean (
